added.name: Rodeo Robotics
added.long_description:
Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time.

Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention.

They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns.

Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles.

Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.

added.name: ChemPilot.ai
added.long_description:
We use AI and quantum-based simulations to discover and develop new materials for defense and dual-use applications, from energetics and propellants to carbon fibers, polymers, coatings and composites. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial-and-error lab work. We compress that to months, using physics-based simulation, machine learning and AI agents that only send labs candidates that can actually be made.

Sam, Ofir and Maor have spent the past two years researching the discovery of these exact materials together at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring deep expertise in chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, and the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that work.

The defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains, from energetics and propellants to carbon fibers, high-temperature composites and specialty polymers. Demand for new capabilities is surging, and materials take decades to develop. The West needs new materials it can make securely, fast and cheap - ChemPilot will help find and develop them.

long_description.before: Output is a fully integrated AI lab building Artificial General Biological Intelligence, from the molecular level up to whole systems. The discovery of new biology and the design of therapeutic moonshots become routine.
long_description.after: Output Labs is a frontier AI research lab. We created Mechanistic Reasoning, a new kind of AI that learns how and why complex systems work. It lets us understand the systems behind science's hardest problems, and control them.

one_liner.before: The foundation for the next era of biology
one_liner.after: The foundation for the next era of science

long_description.before:
While building WeReno.com, we managed over $1B in renovations and noticed something: property owners kept coming back long after projects ended. We realized buildings have no memory, and every repair, maintenance issue, and service request starts from scratch.

So we built Handyman.ai, an AI agent that remembers your property, anticipates problems, and handles everything from maintenance to repairs.

In our first three months, we've facilitated $10M in GMV, validating the opportunity to build an AI agent for every property.

long_description.before: stagewise is building the open-source agentic IDE: a developer workspace for creating and orchestrating coding agents, previewing running apps, and managing Git workflows. Developers can run agents in parallel, use their preferred models or existing coding subscriptions, and keep agents connected to browser/runtime context as well as the broader codebase, from APIs and tests to docs and deployment paths.
long_description.after:
stagewise is building Klex Bots, autonomous AI coworkers that can take on real work inside companies.

Unlike traditional AI assistants, Klex Bots don't need to be prompted for every task. They operate continuously, maintain their own memory and workspaces, and use the same tools and systems as human employees. They can execute complex, multi-step tasks independently, collaborate with other bots or humans, and can use multiple sandboxes/computers depending on configuration.

Our Klex Cloud platform makes it easy for businesses to deploy and manage these digital coworkers securely, using their preferred AI models and infrastructure, hosting agents either in cloud or on custom infrastructure.

one_liner.after: The makers of Klex Bots, your own team of digital coworkers.

long_description.before:
Moda is a harness engineering platform. It turns production traces into verified improvements for your agent harness: prompts, tools, skills, evals, and memory.

The infra problems we actually take: transfer what a frontier model learned onto an open-source one without losing performance, and stand up a model router for your own system and task. Same loop both times. Name the layer that broke, ship the change, replay it on old traffic before it goes out. We've built the infrastructure to tackle these harness problems at scale.

We do not sell a platform that solves every harness problem. We sell those jobs, on an agent already in production.
long_description.after: Your agents should never make the same mistake twice. Moda helps you engineer better agents from production data. Find recurring failures, understand what caused them, and build evals from real agent runs. Compare models on the tasks your users actually need. Test changes to your prompts, tools, and workflows against past production traffic before you ship. Know what broke, what to change, and whether the fix worked.

one_liner.before: Harness Engineering Infrastructure that developers love.
one_liner.after: Your agents should never make the same mistake twice.

long_description.before:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patent-pending system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

long_description.before: OpEra is the AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets. Companies with physical operations make thousands of decisions every day, and we help their teams make the best one at every step from production to delivery: (1) Planning: how much to make, buy and stock. (2) Scheduling: what runs when, and who works on what. (3) Allocation: which warehouse or store gets each order. (4) Routing: boat, plane or truck, and which route each one takes. Founded out of MIT's Operations Research Center.
